_comment: Action registry. Each entry references an NPC key from _maps/npcs/registry.json and lists their actions. Use _action_templates as reference for authoring new actions.
Taterzens paths are set exclusively in-game via the path editor.
Enter editor: /npc edit path  |  Exit editor: /npc edit path  |  Clear: /npc edit path clear
In the editor, left-click a block to add it as a node (turns red); right-click to remove.
The 'waypoints' array below is a planning reference — use these coordinates to know where to click in-game.
Fallback (single destination, no loop): /npc action goto <x> <y> <z>
Sets the NPC's movement behaviour.
Types: NONE | FORCED_LOOK | FORCED_PATH | PATH | FOLLOW | FREE
FORCED_LOOK: looks at players within 4 blocks.
PATH: follows path with rests and look-arounds.
FORCED_PATH: follows path strictly, no rests.
FOLLOW: pursues a target. Requires 'target' field (name or UUID).
FREE: wanders freely inside an enclosed area.
NONE: stationary.
Runs a give command when a player right-clicks the NPC.
--clicker-- is replaced at runtime with the interacting player's name.
Permission level must be >= 2 for the give command to execute.
Set permission level: /npc edit commands setPermissionLevel 2
Starts a Blabber dialog when a player right-clicks the NPC.
target: '--clicker--' for the interacting player, or any selector for someone else.
interlocutor: selector for the NPC entity itself (optional but recommended for @interlocutor use in dialog).
Dialog file must exist at: data/luminacion/blabber/dialogues/<dialog_name>.json
Permission level must be >= 2.
Set permission level: /npc edit commands setPermissionLevel 2
blabber_dialog._command: /npc edit commands add blabber dialogue start luminacion:<dialog_name> --clicker-- @e[type=<type>,limit=1,sort=nearest]

_comment: Convention for pausing a roaming NPC's routine while it's talking to a player,
and resuming it afterwards. Applies to any NPC whose movement mode isn't NONE.
Files involved:
functions/npcs/_shared/pause_routine.mcfunction   — shared, sets movement NONE + tags 'luminacion.paused'
functions/npcs/_shared/enter_dialog.mcfunction    — shared, calls pause_routine + tags 'luminacion.in_dialog'
functions/npcs/_template/resume_routine.mcfunction   — per NPC, restores this NPC's movement mode
functions/npcs/_template/check_proximity.mcfunction  — per NPC, tick-based stop/resume within 2 blocks
functions/npcs/_template/end_with_gift.mcfunction    — per NPC, pattern for endings combining give+resume
data/luminacion/tags/functions/npc_routine_tick.json — registry: add each NPC's check_proximity.mcfunction here
Setup for a given NPC:
1. Right-click actions (spawn.mcfunction) start with:
npc edit commands add function luminacion:npcs/_shared/enter_dialog
before 'blabber dialogue start ...'.
2. Every end_dialogue state in that NPC's dialogs calls (directly, or via a
combined-effect function like end_with_gift.mcfunction):
execute as @interlocutor run function luminacion:npcs/<npc_key>/resume_routine
3. Duplicate resume_routine.mcfunction and check_proximity.mcfunction into
functions/npcs/<npc_key>/, and register check_proximity.mcfunction in
npc_routine_tick.json.
Why both an end_dialogue action AND a tick-based check: Blabber does not run
end_dialogue actions if the player exits the dialog early (Escape / disconnect),
so the tick check (stop within 2 blocks, resume once no player is within 2 blocks
and not mid-dialog) is the safety net that guarantees the NPC never gets stuck
paused. Confirmed from Blabber's PlayerDialogueTracker source.
Reads or writes a variable using scoreboard objectives.
Two objectives are used as data types:
luminacion.bool  — dummy objective, values: 0 (false) or 1 (true)
luminacion.int   — dummy objective, any integer value
The score holder name IS the variable name (fake player convention).
Operations: set | add | subtract | reset | test (compare)
Example: scoreboard players set quest_started luminacion.bool 1
These objectives must be initialised once via load function:
scoreboard objectives add luminacion.bool dummy
scoreboard objectives add luminacion.int dummy
